sources.title: Repository ByteDance frontend interview source containing the usePrevious prompt

claims.text: The source asks for a custom usePrevious Hook that records the prior State value; the UI-triggering extension is a separate follow-up prompt.
The classic interview implementation uses a persistent ref and an Effect that records current value after commit; ref mutation itself does not trigger rendering.
Initial undefined, same-value, and object-reference cases match the documented previous-commit lifecycle model in both writer and independent validation.

Current React documentation says ref.current changes do not re-render and cautions against reading/writing refs during render, so the answer explicitly limits the pattern rather than presenting it as universal production best practice.

validation.command: extract exact candidate JavaScript; independent static contract check plus 4 deterministic and 1000 randomized render/commit lifecycle-model sequences
validation.reported_stdout: PASS exact_hook=useRef+useEffect deterministic=4 randomized=1000 initial=undefined previous_commit_model=pass same_value=pass object_identity=pass
checks: ref write occurs inside useEffect with [value]
A -> B -> C yields undefined, A, B
same-value renders retain the immediately preceding render value
object identity is preserved by reference
1000 independent randomized value sequences match the previous-commit model

findings: The candidate stays on the preserved usePrevious hand-write prompt and does not silently merge the separate follow-up question that asks for UI-triggering updates.
The implementation is complete and uses the expected useRef plus post-commit Effect timing: a render consumes the stored value before the Effect records the current value for a later render.
Initial undefined semantics, same-value renders, and object-reference behavior are stated explicitly instead of being left as hidden assumptions.
The answer correctly states that changing ref.current does not trigger a React re-render and therefore does not present ref as a replacement for render-driving state.

The current React documentation caveat against treating ref.current as a general render-time data source is surfaced explicitly, so the classic interview pattern is not overstated as universal production best practice.
Independent deterministic and randomized lifecycle-model checks agree with the candidate explanation and exact code structure.
The project section remains hypothetical and contains no fabricated production claim.
